incidents.symptom: Harness accepted invalid VERIFIED metadata and returned release PASS for a P0 risk using README as regressionTest and NOT_RUN as review evidence.
incidents.rootCause: Completion gate checked only path existence and truthy reviewer/evidence; it did not require a test file, actual PASS evidence or distinct reviewer.
incidents.resolution: Require an internal regular test file, concrete regression/review metadata, normalized distinct implementer/reviewer, review timestamp and commit; fail closed for invalid release records.
incidents.prevention: Never mark VERIFIED without execution evidence and independent review; keep adversarial completion regressions.

incidents.symptom: Harness accepted incident records without occurrence time, resolution or REAL/SYNTHETIC distinction and accepted invalid loggedAt.
incidents.rootCause: Incident required-field list did not include occurrence time or resolution, and timestamps were only checked as nonblank strings.
incidents.resolution: Require occurredAt, loggedAt ISO roundtrip validation, resolution and recordType; CLI exposes occurrence/resolution and creates OPEN records only.
incidents.prevention: Keep required-field and impossible-date regression cases; synthetic journals remain isolated.

incidents.symptom: Harness stored JSON-shaped synthetic credentials and accepted credentials inserted directly into the journal; initial patch still missed nested JSON text in three regression cases.
incidents.rootCause: Credential regex was CLI-only and did not handle quoted JSON keys or nested string escaping.
incidents.resolution: Share recursive credential validation across CLI and inventories, cover JSON/Basic/URL/private-key patterns, and report generic errors without echoing values.
incidents.prevention: Redact before recording; test rejected inputs leave journal bytes unchanged; pattern scanning remains defense in depth.

incidents.symptom: Preflight allowed case-varied environment/key paths, several SSH/service-account key names and invalid external browser JavaScript syntax. Fresh Reviewer also found uppercase .JS bypass in the first patch.
incidents.rootCause: Filename regex was case-sensitive and narrow; syntax checking covered only server.js and inline browser scripts. The first patch's tracked JS extension filter remained case-sensitive.
incidents.resolution: Use NUL-delimited Git filenames and case-insensitive sensitive basename matching; syntax-check all tracked js/mjs/cjs with node --check. Match JavaScript extensions case-insensitively.
incidents.prevention: Keep tracked secret filename and external/harness syntax regression cases; no product code is executed.
incidents.evidence: Original 6d4b82145e606a25caabeed9fbfad6fe19e9554a; integration-probes-initial.json: five filename guards and external browser syntax guard failed. Fresh Reviewer d25b fixture public/fresh.JS with invalid syntax exited 0; preserved in fresh-review-d25b.json.

incidents.symptom: Fresh Reviewer found that array-valued IDs and verificationCommit could pass string regex checks; malformed blocker IDs could also crash release CLI.
incidents.rootCause: JavaScript regex coerced arrays into matching strings; release display assumed every blocker ID was a string.
incidents.resolution: Require primitive string IDs and verificationCommit; use safe labels for invalid blocker IDs and add schema plus CLI regressions.
incidents.prevention: Test wrong JSON value types with otherwise complete evidence and require structured FAIL instead of unhandled exceptions.
